title: Series and parallel: AND and OR with contacts
summary: Combine contacts in series for AND and in parallel for OR, read a truth table, and finish a program with a horn that sounds when either of two conditions is true.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real alarm horn or overheat sensor behaves.
objectives: Explain that contacts in series pass power only when all of them conduct (AND), and contacts in parallel pass power when any of them conducts (OR).
Change a rung so that a horn sounds in every situation a sentence of the machine names, and check it against every row of a truth table.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/SeriesParallel.ld.json two rungs are drawn. The first lights RunLamp when Auto and Ready are both TRUE, with two contacts in series. The second sounds Horn, but it only reads DoorOpen. Make the horn sound when DoorOpen is TRUE, when Overheat is TRUE, or when both are.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which rule of this program needs both of its conditions and which one needs only one of them.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict RunLamp and Horn. At {{t:20}} ms Auto and Ready are both TRUE. At {{t:50}} ms only Overheat is TRUE. What are the two outputs at each time?
stages.checkpoint: {{v:SeriesParallel.RunLamp=true,SeriesParallel.Horn=false@20|RunLamp ON, Horn OFF}} at {{t:20}} ms; {{v:SeriesParallel.RunLamp=false,SeriesParallel.Horn=true@50|RunLamp OFF, Horn ON}} at {{t:50}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program reads only DoorOpen in the horn rung, so Horn stays OFF at {{t:50}} ms although Overheat is TRUE. Change it so that Horn is ON whenever DoorOpen or Overheat is TRUE, and OFF only when both are FALSE. Leave the RunLamp rung as it is.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, which tries the combinations of the truth table one step at a time, and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named SeriesParallel and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:40}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:60}} ms: Horn is ON when only DoorOpen is TRUE, when only Overheat is TRUE and when both are TRUE. It is OFF when neither is. RunLamp is ON only at {{t:20}} ms, when both Auto and Ready are TRUE.
stages.checkpoint: RunLamp rises once at {{t:20}} ms, and Horn stays ON from {{t:40}} ms to {{t:60}} ms.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Put DoorOpen and Overheat in series instead and watch which assertion fails. Which rows of the truth table does that change?
stages.checkpoint: In series the horn needs both inputs, so it falls silent at {{t:40}} ms and {{t:50}} ms, the two rows where only one input is TRUE; only the row where both are TRUE keeps it ON.

hints.text: Look at the horn rung: list the situations in which power must reach Horn, and count the ways the rung gives it to reach the coil now.
Add a normally open contact on Overheat in the second row, under the DoorOpen contact, and join it to the first row so the two are in parallel. Leave the RunLamp rung as it is.

faultCases: The starting program reads only DoorOpen in the horn rung, so Horn stays OFF at {{t:50}} ms although Overheat is TRUE.
